newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks close mixed ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: China stocks close mixed ahead of holiday.

text.p: China's A and B shares closed mixed on Wednesday with most investors on the sidelines ahead of the lunar new year holiday, brokers said.
Shanghai's foreign currency B share index inched up 0.037 points, or 0.06 percent, to 65.438 while Shenzhen's B index shed 0.47 points, or 0.3 percent, to close at 152.7.
Brokers said the indices would continue to consolidate at current levels ahead of the two-week lunar new year holiday which for the exchange begins on February 3.
"The holiday mood dominated recent trading given a lack of market-moving news," a Shanghai broker said.
On the Shanghai B market, food producer Shanghai Dajiang was the star on speculative buying, rising $0.036, or 6.64 percent, to $0.578 on volume of 144,800 shares.
Shanghai Narcissus Electric Appliances followed on bargain-hunting on the heaviest volume of 2.3 million shares traded, up $0.008, or 4.34 percent, to $0.192.
On Shenzhen's B share market, Lionda, a conglomerate with brewery interests, was the sharpest loser and dipped HK$0.10, or 2.41 percent, to HK$4.05 on trade of 269,920 shares.
Property developer Hainan Pearl River, the biggest gainer, maintained its powerful upward momentum on speculation by institutions that it will post strong 1996 results.
It rose HK$0.26, or 7.03 percent, to HK$3.96 on the day's heaviest trade of 3.88 million shares.
Shanghai's domestic A share index edged up 6.21 points, or 0.62 percent, to 1004.17 but Shenzhen's A index slipped 0.15 points, or 0.04 percent, to finish at 370.00.
In Shanghai, retailer Beijing Wangfujing was the star on institutional buying, surging 0.92 yuan, or 10 percent, to its limit-up of 10.12 yuan after 12.1 million shares were traded.
On the Shenzhen A market, worst performer Shenbao sank 0.50 yuan, or 2.78 percent, to 17.46 yuan on profit-taking, brokers said.
